header: Date: 2027-04-08 | Time: 08:00 PT | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Jordan, Maya, Samir (Redwood) + Dr. Emily Carter, Liam, Nora, Ava (HavenWell)
summary: Kickoff for HavenWell Health onboarding to Redwood Inference. Covered account setup, SSO/SCIM, security and compliance artifacts, deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), pilot success criteria, initial integration steps, and timeline. Agreed owners and dates for key action items and scheduled a technical deep-dive next week to run benchmarks and scoping.
topics: Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC)
transcript:
00:00 Jordan: Okay everyone good to start? Uh yeah thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE and I'll run the kickoff. Hello!
00:12 Maya: Hey all, Maya CSM here, quick intro then we'll cover the onboarding flow.
00:20 Dr. Emily Carter: Hi it's Emily Carter, Head of Data at HavenWell. Thanks for setting this up.
00:26 Liam Brooks: Liam, CTO, I'll mostly listen and follow up on infra bits.
00:31 Nora Diaz: Nora, Compliance. I'll have questions on retention and SOC2.
00:35 Ava Simmons: Ava, DevOps. I'll handle network and VPC.
00:40 Jordan: Great. Agenda — quick intros, what success looks like, security/compliance ask, provisioning and SSO, deployment options, pilot scope, next steps. Any additions?
00:55 Liam: Sounds good. Curious about latency targets and cost tradeoffs — that's top of mind.
01:02 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll cover p95 latency expectations and cost estimates.
01:15 Samir: Hi everyone, Samir on Solutions Eng, I'll do the tech deep-dive next week.
01:22 Jordan: Quick question for Emily — what are your immediate success criteria for a pilot?
01:30 Dr. Emily Carter: We want a safe way to test patient-facing summarization, so accuracy/quality first, then latency under 250ms p95 ideally, and clear audit logs for any PHI touch points.
01:45 Jordan: Noted. On privacy — Redwood supports private deployments and has audit logging, we'll share the SOC2 and security pack after this.
01:55 Nora: Can you clarify encryption at rest and key management? We use AWS KMS currently, need customer-managed keys.
02:04 Maya: Yes we have KMS integrations and customer-managed key options for Private; for Hosted we offer application-level encryption and we can do envelope encryption with your KMS for certain tiers.
02:18 Nora: Okay that's promising, we'll need details.
02:25 Ava: For network, do you support VPC peering or private link?
02:30 Samir: We support VPC peering and private link for Private deployment and Dedicated can be put into customer VPCs in many regions; we'll need your network team to share CIDR lists and allowlist.
02:44 Ava: Cool. I'll collect that.
02:50 Jordan: On provisioning — typical flow: we invite 5 users initially, SCIM for groups later. SSO via SAML or OIDC, SCIM user provisioning optional. How do you manage identities?
03:05 Liam: We use Okta for identity, SCIM would be ideal eventually but initial SAML is fine.
03:12 Jordan: Okta is in our standard docs — we'll send SSO setup guide.
03:18 Dr. Emily Carter: Regarding data retention, we need 7 year retention policies for logs and ability to disable retention for PHI transcripts or flag them. How flexible is retention?
03:30 Maya: We can configure retention buckets; for Private deployments you control retention entirely. For hosted we have configurable retention policies and can do no-retention options on request with an enterprise add-on. We'll put specifics in the doc.
03:45 Nora: Also need audit trails for who accessed logs and model outputs.
03:50 Samir: Audit logs include token-level metadata, user IDs, timestamps — we'll share sample schema but actual fields depend on deployment mode.
03:58 Jordan: On the deployment decision — we recommend starting hosted for speed if data residency isn't blocking, otherwise Dedicated or Private if you need isolation or KMS control. Thoughts?
04:14 Liam: Our legal/compliance leans towards Dedicated or Private because of PHI; hosted is risky unless we get extra contractual terms.
04:25 Jordan: Understood. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and isolation without full private control; Private is full VPC/on-prem. Both can integrate with your KMS.
04:36 Samir: For Dedicated we can size GPU pool for expected concurrency; we can run a cost model during scoping.
04:44 Dr. Emily Carter: On model selection — we care about hallucination rates for summaries. Can we pin model versions and run A/B?
04:54 Samir: Yes, you can pin versions and we support canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to another model variant. We'll set up an eval harness to track quality regressions.
05:08 Jordan: Pilot scope idea — 2-week pilot with production-like traffic to the summarization endpoint, run our evals on a set of 200 prompt examples, track ROUGE/QA and latency, then decide capacity. Is that acceptable?
05:24 Dr. Emily Carter: That works. We'll also want integration to the EHR system but start with sampled documents.
05:33 Ava: For EHR integration we may need private endpoints; depends on data flow.
05:38 Samir: We'll design a staging pipeline to strip PHI if needed and test with synthetic data first.
05:48 Jordan: On training and enablement — we offer two 1-hour workshops: platform basics and operations/alerts. We'll schedule those after initial provisioning.
05:58 Maya: And we'll assign a dedicated CSM (that's me) as the point of contact for success checks.
06:06 Nora: Good. Also need SOW and pricing breakdown to present to procurement.
06:12 Jordan: We'll send pricing estimates and a sample SOW.
06:18 Liam: One question — how do you handle model updates and regressions in production?
06:25 Samir: Platform supports model versioning, automatic canary, evaluative regression alerts tied to prompt sets. There's a rollback mechanism and automatic fallback to a stable variant.
06:36 Dr. Emily Carter: Great. For compliance review we'll need the full data flow diagram and encryption details.
06:43 Maya: We'll include those in the security package.
06:48 Jordan: Any blockers to start provisioning this week?
06:52 Ava: I can provide network contacts and Okta config by Monday.
06:57 Nora: Compliance will review SOC2 docs — timeline dependent but we can start.
07:03 Liam: Procurement needs SOW and pricing to move forward.
07:08 Jordan: We'll send those by Friday.
07:12 Samir: For next week tech deep-dive, we'll run a small latency benchmark and a sample eval. Are you ok with 2027-04-15 14:00 PT?
07:21 Dr. Emily Carter: Yes that's good.
07:25 Jordan: Cool. Quick recap then next steps: Jordan to send playbook, Maya to send compliance pack, Samir to scope Dedicated vs Private costs and perf, Ava to share network details, set tech deep-dive 4/15. Anything else?
07:44 Nora: Please include data deletion SLA in the SOW.
07:48 Jordan: Noted. We'll add data deletion SLA language.
07:52 Liam: Also can you include expected token pricing in the estimate and any overage behavior?
07:57 Jordan: Yep we'll include token pricing tiers, reserved capacity pricing and overage rules.
08:03 Dr. Emily Carter: Thanks all. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
08:07 Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and invites. Meeting adjourned.
08:12 Speaker 6: [brief crosstalk] okay bye
notes: References: onboarding playbook link (shared post call), SOC2 packet, pricing spreadsheet and SOW template referenced.
